newsitem.title: USA: UAL, pilots in talks on regional jets.
newsitem.headline: UAL, pilots in talks on regional jets.

text.p: The pilots union at United Airlines said it is in talks with the company to determine which pilots will fly new regional jets the airline wants to buy to feed its hub operations and add service to smaller markets.

In a recorded message to its members, the pilots union said the recent talks focused on job protection, protection against furloughs, and feeder airline partners controlling the amount of flying. The negotiations have also addressed tying growth at United to any growth of the feeder airlines' regional jet operations, the union said.
Last month, the union reaffirmed its position that it wants United's mainline pilots, not commuter airline pilots, to fly the regional jets.
Representatives for UAL Corp's United Airlines could not be reached for comment.
United's Chairman Gerald Greenwald told the Washington Post last month that he expected a solution would be reached with the pilots' union to allow the commuter carriers to fly the jets.
Several commuter airlines operate under the United Express name. These airlines are not owned by UAL but use the brandname under a marketing agreement.
